# Captain Jim

## Overview

- **Age:** Seventy-six years old  <sub>[v4 c8 P63](../source/v04-c08.md#nw-v04-c08-p0063)</sub>
- **Gender:** Male  <sub>[v4 c6 P14](../source/v04-c06.md#nw-v04-c06-p0014)</sub>
- **Status:** Deceased  <sub>[v4 c39 P28](../source/v04-c39.md#nw-v04-c39-p0028)</sub>
- **Origin:** Prince Edward Island  <sub>[v4 c7 P5](../source/v04-c07.md#nw-v04-c07-p0005)</sub>
- **Role:** Lighthouse keeper on Four Winds Point  <sub>[v4 c2 P23](../source/v04-c02.md#nw-v04-c02-p0023)</sub>
- **Titles:** Captain  <sub>[v4 c6 P10](../source/v04-c06.md#nw-v04-c06-p0010)</sub>
- **Nicknames:** Captain Jim  <sub>[v4 c6 P10](../source/v04-c06.md#nw-v04-c06-p0010)</sub>

## Appearance

Captain Jim is a tall, ungainly man, somewhat stooped yet suggestive of great strength and endurance. He has a clean-shaven, bronzed face deeply lined with age, a thick mane of iron-gray hair falling to his shoulders, and deep-set, blue eyes. As he grows older, his hair becomes grayer, and he appears increasingly frail and bent.

_Sources: [v4 c6 P14](../source/v04-c06.md#nw-v04-c06-p0014), [v4 c30 P3](../source/v04-c30.md#nw-v04-c30-p0003), [v4 c30 P11](../source/v04-c30.md#nw-v04-c30-p0011)_

## Personality

Captain Jim is a simple-minded, high-souled man who remains placid, cheerful, and eternally youthful in heart. He possesses a deep, inner joy and passion for beauty in all things, enjoying life chronically despite hardship. He delights in philosophical discussions, storytelling, and meddling in good causes, showing great kindness and understanding to others.

_Sources: [v4 c6 P14](../source/v04-c06.md#nw-v04-c06-p0014), [v4 c8 P61](../source/v04-c08.md#nw-v04-c08-p0061), [v4 c9 P5](../source/v04-c09.md#nw-v04-c09-p0005), [v4 c9 P38](../source/v04-c09.md#nw-v04-c09-p0038), [v4 c14 P3](../source/v04-c14.md#nw-v04-c14-p0003), [v4 c17 P16](../source/v04-c17.md#nw-v04-c17-p0016), [v4 c17 P18](../source/v04-c17.md#nw-v04-c17-p0018)_

## History

Born James Boyd, Captain Jim spent his youth on Prince Edward Island listening to poetry recited by schoolmaster John Selwyn. Descended from seafarers, he ran off to sea as a boy and spent fifty years sailing across the globe. Over fifty years before meeting Anne Blythe, he lost his sweetheart Margaret in a sudden storm at sea, spending months searching the shore for her body in vain. During his travels he rescued an amnesiac named Dick Moore in Cuba and brought him back to his wife Leslie. Retiring from the sea, he became the lighthouse keeper at Four Winds Point, befriending his companion cat, the First Mate. He built close friendships with the residents of the area, including Anne Blythe, Gilbert Blythe, Cornelia Bryant, and Owen Ford, with whom he collaborated to write his life's stories in a book titled The Life-Book of Captain Jim. He passed away peacefully in his sleep shortly before the publication of his book.

_Sources: [v4 c2 P23](../source/v04-c02.md#nw-v04-c02-p0023), [v4 c7 P5](../source/v04-c07.md#nw-v04-c07-p0005), [v4 c7 P48](../source/v04-c07.md#nw-v04-c07-p0048), [v4 c8 P63](../source/v04-c08.md#nw-v04-c08-p0063), [v4 c9 P38](../source/v04-c09.md#nw-v04-c09-p0038), [v4 c11 P35](../source/v04-c11.md#nw-v04-c11-p0035), [v4 c13 P15](../source/v04-c13.md#nw-v04-c13-p0015), [v4 c20 P16](../source/v04-c20.md#nw-v04-c20-p0016), [v4 c20 P17](../source/v04-c20.md#nw-v04-c20-p0017), [v4 c24 P11](../source/v04-c24.md#nw-v04-c24-p0011), [v4 c25 P6](../source/v04-c25.md#nw-v04-c25-p0006), [v4 c39 P5](../source/v04-c39.md#nw-v04-c39-p0005), [v4 c39 P28](../source/v04-c39.md#nw-v04-c39-p0028)_

## Background by volume

- Descended from a race of sea-going people  <sub>[v4 c7 P5](../source/v04-c07.md#nw-v04-c07-p0005)</sub>
- Ran off to sea as a boy of sixteen  <sub>[v4 c7 P5](../source/v04-c07.md#nw-v04-c07-p0005), [v4 c7 P48](../source/v04-c07.md#nw-v04-c07-p0048)</sub>
- Lost his sweetheart Margaret at sea over fifty years prior  <sub>[v4 c20 P16](../source/v04-c20.md#nw-v04-c20-p0016)</sub>
- Searched the shore for months for Margaret's body  <sub>[v4 c20 P17](../source/v04-c20.md#nw-v04-c20-p0017)</sub>
- Sailed all his life until retiring five years prior to meeting Anne  <sub>[v4 c8 P63](../source/v04-c08.md#nw-v04-c08-p0063)</sub>
- Traveled all over the world collecting stories and curios  <sub>[v4 c8 P63](../source/v04-c08.md#nw-v04-c08-p0063), [v4 c9 P46](../source/v04-c09.md#nw-v04-c09-p0046), [v5 c2 P69](../source/v05-c02.md#nw-v05-c02-p0069)</sub>
- Rescued a neglected cat, naming him the First Mate  <sub>[v4 c9 P38](../source/v04-c09.md#nw-v04-c09-p0038)</sub>
- Discovered the amnesiac Dick Moore in Cuba and brought him home  <sub>[v4 c11 P35](../source/v04-c11.md#nw-v04-c11-p0035), [v4 c13 P15](../source/v04-c13.md#nw-v04-c13-p0015)</sub>

## Quotes

> Captain Jim is my week-a-day name and you might as well begin as you’re sartain to end up—calling me that.  <sub>[v4 c6 P10](../source/v04-c06.md#nw-v04-c06-p0010)</sub>

> I’ve kind of contracted a habit of enj’ying things. It’s got so chronic that I believe I even enj’y the disagreeable things. It’s great fun thinking they can’t last.  <sub>[v4 c17 P18](../source/v04-c17.md#nw-v04-c17-p0018)</sub>

> The sea took her from me, but some day I’ll find her. Mistress Blythe. It can’t keep us apart forever.  <sub>[v4 c20 P17](../source/v04-c20.md#nw-v04-c20-p0017)</sub>

> I’ve been all over the world, Mistress Blythe, and take it all in all, I’ve never seen a finer sight than a summer sunrise over the gulf. A man can’t pick his time for dying, Mistress Blythe—jest got to go when the Great Captain gives His sailing orders.  <sub>[v4 c35 P34](../source/v04-c35.md#nw-v04-c35-p0034)</sub>
